apps.notes: Taiga is split across repos: taigaio/taiga-back (Django API/core, LICENSE = MPL 2.0, file headers 'Mozilla Public License, v. 2.0') and taigaio/taiga-front (Angular web client, LICENSE = GNU AGPL v3, headers say 'GNU Affero General Public License' with no 'or later' -> AGPL-3.0-only); taigaio/taiga-docker is the official install (MPL-2.0). taiga-back chosen as the canonical repo. kaleidos-ventures/taiga ('Taiga next') last pushed 2023-12 and is not the current product. Activity: taiga-back 36 commits since 2026-03-24 (security and bug fixes, a GitHub attachments feature), taiga-front 21. Screenshot: tree.taiga.io is Taiga's own hosted web app; Taiga's own public project has kanban turned off and an empty backlog, so a public, archived community project (TransforMap) was captured anonymously; the pink 'This project was archived. It is now read-only.' bar is real app UI for that project; the cookie banner was hidden. taiga.io's own screenshots are 640px wide and unreadable. API docs docs.taiga.io/api.html, webhooks docs.taiga.io/webhooks.html; plugins via taiga-contrib-* repos.

apps.name: Tasks.md
apps.tagline: A self-hosted kanban board that saves every card as a Markdown file in a folder.

license.name: MIT License

mobile.how: No app; the web app can be installed as a PWA on a phone

mcp.note: We found no MCP server. Because cards are plain Markdown files, any file-system MCP server can read and edit them.

screenshot.source: Captured from a local install of Tasks.md 3.3.0

apps.notes: LICENSE MIT. Latest release 3.3.0 on 2026-03-08 (about 6.5 months ago; releases every 1-2 months through 2025-2026); README says 'This is a low maintenance project' with a deliberately narrow scope — status could reasonably be 'maintenance' if no release lands soon. Only official screenshot is the README demo.gif (800x328, unreadable), so I ran tag 3.3.0 from source locally (same steps as its Dockerfile/entrypoint; Docker Desktop storage was failing), created 3 lanes and 7 cards with tags through the real UI, and captured light and dark (app follows the OS theme). Homepage on GitHub points to Docker Hub; website set to the repo. No documented API (the backend has internal HTTP endpoints only). Official Docker image baldissaramatheus/tasks.md. MCP: gh search for 'tasks.md mcp'/'tasksmd' found nothing.

apps.name: Leantime
apps.tagline: A self-hosted project tool with kanban, Gantt and timesheets, plus a personal My Work page and calendar.

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 only

mobile.how: No mobile app; use the web app in a phone browser

mcp.note: Official MCP server is a paid plugin (beta) from the Leantime marketplace, with the Leantime/leantime-mcp bridge for stdio clients. A free community option is daniel-eder/leantime-mcp.

apps.caveat: Some add-ons, including the MCP server, are paid plugins.

screenshot.source: Official screenshot from the project's README, © the Leantime project

apps.notes: LICENSE is GNU AGPL v3; composer.json 'license': 'AGPL-3.0-only'. README exception: plugins in /app/Plugins may be under other licenses including the enterprise license. README feature table says all listed features (kanban, Gantt, table, list and calendar views, timesheets, goals, docs/wikis) are in the OSS version. Planner angle: the screenshot is the 'My Work' dashboard with personal to-dos and a day calendar; README also shows timesheets and a personal calendar — worth a mention in a planner post. API is JSON-RPC 2.0 (docs.leantime.io/api/usage), not REST, so REST is left out of api[]. Chat notifications go to Slack/Mattermost/Discord; no general webhooks found. demo.leantime.io exists but publishes no login, so it was not used. The README also has an official dark screenshot (dark.png) but it is an older My Work layout, not the same screen, so no dark image. MCP: marketplace.leantime.io/product/mcp-server (paid, beta, Leantime 3.7.3+); support article support.leantime.io/en/article/leantime-mcp-server-dkomm9/. v3.10.0 released 2026-09-24.
